target_customer: Public sector procurement teams (cities, school boards, universities), later private enterprises
problem: Government RFPs and bids were run on paper, email and Excel, which was slow and hard to evaluate.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for sourcing, RFP and bid management

founders.name: Corry Flatt
founders.background_notes: Entrevestor (2015-07-06) says he was a marketer focused on startups, frustrated by paper RFPs.

founders.name: Alex Millar
founders.background_notes: Listed as cofounder and CTO on YC page; no further background found.

exit.reason: Reported price US$108 million (CA$140 million) by a law firm announcement seen in search results.

technical_complexity.rationale: Workflow software for RFP creation, supplier submission and evaluation; standard web SaaS, with effort in security and public sector compliance.

defensibility.rationale: Public sector contracts, procurement records and process integration create stickiness, but features were copyable by larger suites.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: YC description says Bonfire went beyond basic eProcurement suites. Bonfire was acquired by GTY Technology in 2019 and now operates as Euna Procurement.

market_need_then: Entrevestor (2015-07-06) reported more than 60 public sector clients including the Chicago Public School Board and the University of Alberta, sales since about January 2014 and a team under 10. Battery Ventures later said Excel was still the main sourcing tool.

branding.domain_note: Used gobonfire.com; gobonfire.com now redirects to eunasolutions.com

identity.voice_and_tone: Modern, paperless, easy to use (Entrevestor 2015, YC page)

rebrands.to: Euna Solutions, with the product later called Euna Procurement
rebrands.why: Parent rebranded in 2023; Bonfire's procurement product folded into the Euna Procurement offering (2024 release).

brand_strength.rationale: Known within public procurement and Waterloo startup press; many unrelated companies share the Bonfire name, and search found no brand press or community.

outcome_analysis: Bonfire sold paperless RFP software to governments, reaching 60 public sector clients on a team under ten in 2015 while saying it could be profitable. It raised a $3M seed and an $8M Series A led by Battery Ventures in June 2017, grew to 95 people, and was acquired by GTY Technology in February 2019 for a reported US$108M. The product now lives as Euna Procurement, so it succeeded through a repeatable public sector sales motion rather than heavy capital.
notes: Betakit headline says $11M raised: it describes the new round led by Battery as part of an $11M total with an $8M Series A and $3M seed, and the summary text is ambiguous about whether the $11M is new; privatecapitaljournal and ZoomInfo (search results) report an $8M Series A in 2017 and a $3M 2016 seed. The 2016 seed date and its investors come from aggregator listings and are lightly verified. Acquisition price and date come from a law firm announcement and a Mergr listing in search results; the lwlaw page returned 404 when opened, so the price is not confirmed by a primary release. Competitor search found no named competitors dated 2015, so the list is empty. Founder education and employers not found.
